findings.where: README.environment.md, "Words used here": 5 more bullets, if the list may grow beyond 20 additions
findings.problem: Five more project terms pass the 4-row rule. They are less urgent, and each has a reason: (1) Harmony: 3 Operators rows; each row already defines it. (2) Launcher wrappers: 11 rows say "the wrappers"; the introduction of section 2 defines them, and `wrapper` in code font means a different script in section 3.3. (3) `tronperf`, `wrapper`: 13 rows; 4 rows define them with 2 different clauses. (4) Model trace: 6 rows; `EXPORT_ONLY` says only "the trace", which elsewhere means a Perfetto trace. (5) Runner class: 7 rows of section 6; 2 different clauses.
findings.evidence: Harmony: src/rinzler.cpp:2016-2020, h/rinzler/token-processor.hpp:276. Launcher wrappers: doc/dice.md:798-803. `tronperf`, `wrapper`: README.perfetto.md:34, README.perfetto.md:97, README.perfetto.md:167. Model trace: ingest/README.md:3, ingest/README.md:170-186. Runner class: doc/slice-benchmark-lifecycle.md:41-46, README.ci.md:451-457
findings.fix:
- **Harmony**: the prompt format of the gpt-oss models. `rinzler` uses it for
  every model whose name contains `gpt-oss`.
- **Launcher wrappers**: the scripts `bin/rinzler` and `bin/runtron`. They
  start the built `rinzler` and `runtron`, through Dice on a shared host. The
  script `perfetto/wrapper` is a different tool.
- **`tronperf`, `wrapper`**: the Perfetto launcher scripts `perfetto/tronperf`
  and `perfetto/wrapper`. Both start the Perfetto programs and record a trace.
  `tronperf` also runs `runtron`. `wrapper` can signal a running program.
- **Model trace**: the PyTorch export of one model. The export step of ingest
  writes it. The ingest program reads it. It is not a Perfetto trace.
- **Runner class**: a group of CI servers of one hardware type. The Slice
  cost-data refresh knows the classes `2x96core` and `2x72core`.

notes:
Short version. The list "Words used here" has 22 terms and needs 20 more: 2 are must-fix (Scheduler; Shared host, legacy host) and 18 are should-fix. No existing term is unused. Four real wording conflicts between rows have exact replacement text.

Method.
- Proposals: the 28 files chunks/*.final.json hold 330 proposed definitions for 252 distinct terms (case and code font ignored). 96 of these terms occur in 4 or more rows, and 21 occur in no row. None of them reached the document: render.py fills the list from work/extra_terms.md, and that file does not exist.
- Row counts: a script counted, for every proposed term, the rows of README.environment.md (529 rows) that contain it. The match is case-insensitive and on the whole phrase, and a plural "s" is allowed.
- Inline definitions: a second script found 103 phrases that carry a defining clause ("X (a ...)", "X, the ...", "X is a ...") in 2 or more rows.
- Every new definition has at most 30 words (a code span counts as 1 word) and was checked against the path:line in "evidence".

How to apply. The 20 bullets can go to their logical places in work/template.md (the "where" of each finding). They can also go as one block into work/extra_terms.md, which render.py appends after the "**CI**" bullet. Suggested order of the full list after the change: `rinzler`, `runtron`, `rinzler_proxy`, `rinzler_host`, `libtron`/`libpos`, Instance, Physical slice, Resource map, FPGA card, Bitfile, Hugepage, Arena allocator/legacy allocator, NUMA node, KV cache, KV book, Scheduler, Token tree, Forward pass/minibatch, Hardware attention/software attention, Shared thread pool, Speculative decoding, `save_tokens`, Python tokenizer/Rust tokenizer, FUSE stats, Perfetto, `traced`/`traced_probes`, Dice, Shared host/legacy host, Slot, Submission/grant, Slice, LSF, Distributed Dice, Remote build/LSF worker, `sku0`/`sku1`, platformd, Ingest, `gen/`, Nix dev shell, CI, Slice cost-data refresh, Fake/stub.
Keep the inline clauses in the rows. A reader searches for one variable and reads one row.

The 20 bullets as one block:
- **`rinzler_host`**: a build of `rinzler` that runs models on the CPU and
  needs no FPGA card. The `tron-host` package installs it on test and
  development hosts.
- **Physical slice**: one FPGA card with its CPU cores and its memory. An
  instance owns one or more physical slices. Dice calls this unit a slot. It
  is not the tool Slice.
- **Resource map**: the YAML file `resource-map.yaml`. For each server type it
  lists the FPGA cards, the CPU cores and the NUMA nodes. The repository copy
  is `config/resource-map.yaml`.
- **Arena allocator, legacy allocator**: the two allocators for hugepage
  memory. The arena allocator (`pos_heap_v2`) is the build default. The legacy
  allocator is `pos_heap`. `TRON_USE_ARENA_ALLOCATOR` selects one.
- **KV book**: one allocation of KV cache memory. A book holds a whole number
  of pages. One page holds the keys and values of 64 tokens.
- **Scheduler**: in section 1, the part of `rinzler` and `runtron` that keeps
  the token tree and chooses the tokens of each forward pass. Dice and LSF
  have their own schedulers.
- **Token tree**: the tree in which the scheduler stores all token sequences.
  Sequences that start with the same tokens share nodes.
- **Forward pass, minibatch**: a forward pass is one run of the model over a
  group of tokens. A minibatch is a part of that group that the model computes
  together.
- **Shared thread pool**: the worker threads of one process for model work on
  the CPU. In a forward pass, some workers are main helpers for non-attention
  work. The other workers are attention workers.
- **Speculative decoding**: a generation mode in which a small draft model
  proposes a tree of candidate tokens, the draft tree. The main model then
  verifies the tree. See `TRON_USE_SPECULATION`.
- **`save_tokens`**: a request parameter of `rinzler`. When it is `true`, the
  response also holds the rendered prompt, the prompt token ids and the output
  token ids.
- **Python tokenizer, Rust tokenizer**: the two tokenizer implementations. The
  Rust tokenizer is the Hugging Face library inside the process. The Python
  tokenizer is a slower fallback that runs a Python child process.
- **`traced`, `traced_probes`**: the two Perfetto daemons. `traced` is the
  tracing service. Programs send it trace events over a socket.
  `traced_probes` collects kernel events.
- **Shared host, legacy host**: a shared host is a server whose
  `/etc/positron/dice.yaml` sets `mode: shared`. One Dice daemon there queues
  the FPGA work of all users. Other servers are legacy hosts without a Dice
  daemon.
- **Submission, grant**: a submission is one command that a client asks the
  Dice daemon to run. The grant is the slots that the daemon gives to the
  submission while it runs.
- **Distributed Dice**: the part of Dice that runs work on another FPGA server
  through LSF. `bin/dice-lsf-submit` submits the LSF job. The LSF runner
  (`bin/dice-lsf-runner`) starts the work on that server.
- **Remote build, LSF worker**: a remote build is a build that `make` sends to
  an LSF worker through `bin/bsub-build`. An LSF worker is a server that runs
  LSF jobs. `REMOTE=1` selects a remote build.
- **`sku0`, `sku1`**: two server classes of the remote test pool. `sku0` is
  the current AMD Genoa class. `sku1` is the current Intel Granite Rapids
  class. `REMOTE=sku0` or `REMOTE=sku1` selects one.
- **Slice cost-data refresh**: the CI workflow `bench-refresh.yml`. It
  measures the run time and peak memory of each test again. It updates the
  Slice cost data in `config/test-benchmarks.json` through a pull request.
- **Fake, stub**: a short program that a test writes. The code under test runs
  it in place of a real program, for example a fake `mv`.
